title: Work across threads
description:
Write three functions that use threads:

```rust
fn parallel_sum(data: &[u64], threads: usize) -> u64
fn parallel_map<T: Sync, R: Send>(items: &[T], threads: usize, f: impl Fn(&T) -> R + Sync) -> Vec<R>
fn collect_messages(producers: usize, per_producer: usize) -> Vec<String>
```

- `parallel_sum` splits `data` into `threads` nearly equal chunks, sums each on its own scoped thread, and adds the results. `threads` of 0 panics.
- `parallel_map` applies `f` to every item using `threads` scoped threads and returns the results **in input order**.
- `collect_messages` starts `producers` threads; producer `i` sends `"p<i>-<j>"` for `j` in `0..per_producer` over one `mpsc` channel; the function returns everything received, **sorted**.

Use `std::thread::scope` for the first two (so the threads can borrow `data` and `items`), and `std::sync::mpsc` for the third.
hints: Inside `thread::scope(|s| ...)`, `s.spawn(move || ...)` may borrow slices of the outer data, because every scoped thread is joined before `scope` returns.
Join the handles in the order you created them and concatenate their results: the chunks are in order, so the output is too.

In `parallel_map`, every thread needs `f`, but a `move` closure would move `f` into the first thread. Write `let f = &f;` before the scope: each `move` closure then copies the reference (references are `Copy`), and all threads call the same `f`. A chunk size of `(len + threads - 1) / threads` (at least 1) splits the items into `threads` nearly equal parts.
rules: Use scoped threads for parallel_sum and parallel_map.
Use an mpsc channel in collect_messages.

rules.message: Use scoped threads for parallel_sum and parallel_map.
Use an mpsc channel in collect_messages.
